### 2026-11-03: # Research (and planning)

**2.42h**

# Research (and planning)

So I always thought it would be a fun project to make a plotter, so I've decided to try and make one.

I've basically just spent this time looking some stuff up and seeing if it would actually be feasible to make one in budget (could go over, but then its no challenge).

I'm pretty sure I will be able to.

So I was looking at it, and you can actually get 2020 extrusion fairly cheaply, even on Amazon. So I plan to use this as my main building material.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/f50e50b7d2c0533d268c5e8067fff08a8d61126169b220164bc6aa67015de793.png)

I also spent some time planning how I want to lay it out.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/4b3a91caa1a79524f55f67f0fe35a69e6c01883d651b90708fae65bf211ce888.png)

So I'd prefer the design on the left, but then I think I would need 3 steppers, 2 for y, and one for x. But then I should be able to get some really high accelerations. But the cantilevered design on the right would need less materials, but I don't think it will be rigid enough.

I also plan to make it be able to plot on a full piece of A4 paper - on the far right for scale.

And my rough plan for the movement system, is just to use individual axes, instead of a Core XY system, and essentially just have the belt track move next to the 2020 extrusion.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/bbecff057faab9c9831b5c5f3f8292ed585ea0390048c233141b76486d4f4153.png)

I really hope I'll actually be able to make this and finish it, as it might be a bit too ambitious for the time I have.

(I'm thinking Ill custom CAD a frame, joints etc, then either do a custom PCB, or by a shield - whichever is cheaper tbh, then probably just flash like GERBL to it to take normal gcode)

### 2026-11-04: # Stupid amount more of BOM work

**1.3h**

# Stupid amount more of BOM work

I call it BOM work, but it is mostly just seeing what parts I can get away with.

So take the control board for example:

I can either go a premade Arduino board and shield, an ESP32 one, or even go with a custom one. With the only problem being cost.

As much as I'd like to make a fully custom PCB for the controller, I don't think I'll have the budget with all the other parts.

Did find some quite intersting things though:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/e0074423c81a3c34532bc059d14e5f7469a71ea228f3296811cbb379605bc77c.png)

I wish the $1.35 sale price was what it actually sold for - but $10 isnt too bad. except its Arduino, which I dislike. And has pretty rubbish drivers - DRV8825 ones.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/18ccfb4f5d31f850c05ca7e528895404df8990c0302ffcfae8013ad54bfec1a1.png)

So aside from the drivers in this one, it is more what I'd like to have - an esp32, with a better looking board. But ideally I'd also want TMC2209 drivers, but from some reasearch, I dont think the A4988 ones would be too bad - like I mean their much worse, but not the end of the world if I dont have the budget for them.

Also had a decent look into my options into creating a custom PCB, and the cost will just be much higher, especially when having to buy capacitors and resistors. Which you seem to need annoyingly, even if you are just connecting modules.

Although saying that, for the non sale price of some of these things, it could still be worth it:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/228d97d03cf46a81566045f567bf0118324657203a73d73264e95dca9cdf7fde.png)

$15 is alright, but a whole $33? quite literally a third of the budget if I go tier 3.

### 2026-11-05: # Yet more research

**3.6h**

# Yet more research

Seems stupid at this point, spending this long on purely research.

But I think that now I am unlikely to get this project to fit in the $100 budget. Unless I cut features.

## the breakdown

- 2020 extrusion ~$18
- Belt stuff ~$10
- POM Wheels ~$14
- CNC Shield ~$22
- 3x Steppers ~$25

Total: ~$89

Currently are all in the BOM

## research info

might as well say if helps others looking

### 2020 Extrusion

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/907edeff43b1330e8ecabc1f4d961597d2ff44cc0c15b2a11d308620aecf9ed4.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/fad0fc7861ea80ef6df43cabcd11c8088934873f71edb699051f92dad75823da.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/94669bb0d2927b06ade2681c0e517940e93be405d4e45c9a4e6445cc016f822d.png)

Somehow cheaper on Amazon - cheaper than Aliexpress. I'm guessing something to do with shipping and how companies can make their money. But that was an interesting look, as due to shipping, I had to look into a bunch of native UK stores that I'd never heard of before, such as the first OozNest one.

### Belt set

Aliexpress was cheapest, then was just a toss up whether to go individual parts, or a kit, and a kit turned out to be cheaper.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/88b9d2353303dce4052ee2f12b3d5b025d6742335c3f77c1238f46108bebe03a.png)

It's $10 - the $1.35 new shopper price is just a rip off.

### ESP32 CNC shield

think I talked about it last time

the one ive got on the BOM currently is the MKS v2.1, comes with an esp32, and 3 a4988 drivers.

### Nema 17 Steppers

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/07c14558ad00dd580009c26fb5e7d2c16ff35bba6e83c141eb5cc1a48fec3dd0.png)

Actually a pain to look at, especially with the Aliexpress sale prices, but somehow turned out that a store on eBay is better? Although that is in £, so not quite that cheap.

### POM wheels

Just some random ones on Aliexpress which were the cheapest I could find. Was cheaper to get a 24 pack than a 12 pack somehow. (as with my current design, I need probably at least 12 wheels).

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/e2965894fe8fa3b9b55abf63e9ea9d7c63f77793ac575dcc5e700f99b4ae224d.png)

## So the plan

As I'm basically at $90, and havent even factored in the price of the 3D prints, power supply, m5 screws for attachments.

My plan is to drop down to two steppers, with a cantilevered design, as those seem popular.

Was originally less inclined to go this way, as I wanted mine to be more original, but it seems that it is the most popular way for a reason. And it should be rigid enough anyway.

Was originally also half considering making this a laser engraver instead, but theres basically no change I'l have the budget for that.

## tl;dr

Spent a lot of time researching and adding things up for the BOM, and came to the conclusion, that I'll either go over, or have to cut scope to hopefully fit under budget.

### 2026-11-06: # Finally started CAD

**3.67h**

# Finally started CAD

Well I say that, but also did some more BOM work, as I just felt everything should be cheaper.

But am also pretty glad I finally have started designing. I still have no clue where to start, but I've at least laid things out and researched a fair bit.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/d2b7878afa796f22997c231aed0a61ada99c1f1b120cdcb27c2dc66bc0e2fd84.png)

As shown in my lovely drawing, I've decided to sacrifice some rigidity, and go with a cantilevered design. This however does mean I need les POM wheels, less steppers, and less 2020 extrusion - though its somehow still cheapest to buy the same amount of steppers and metal frame thing??

So that means I'll be spending even more time looking at BOM stuff in the future to get things cheaper. But currently I'm at $80, so not too worried, as the rest should mabye fit in the $20.

I know I've probably spent rather long on the BOM, but a plotter for under $100. Is actually pretty insane in my opinion. Thats only £75. Like literally insane. Cheaper than a HP printer somehow.

Well I just hope this optimisation is worth it.

## Actually started CAD

Just some of what I did:

My 2020 extrusion profile - dimensionally accurate where its important lol:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/51762ba45938b81f24fc575af3f56220db9588acfd3150524bcac6410df92eb0.png)

Annoyingly couldn't find and nice 3d models of 2020 extrusion that I liked, so I decided to model it from scratch. With some diagrams that were missing information - well it was just the Amazon page one, I do know that there are better ones online lol.

But anyway, I'd done that, then started modelling. And as I'm a bit too good, I'm just overcomplicating things. So insead of just trying a design, I'm making everything parametric, which starts with just laying things out. So I use joints for that.

And the pain of trying to attach a joint to like a multilayered surface like the bottom of the 2020 extrusion, is a proper pain.

So I did just kinda get rid of it:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/454cfdeb8108a8adb0cdc1cb37491e880ee05f29eee8880b4db79cbe39a5f152.png)

Might end up doing that for the rest as well, depending on how I model things.

And it's only realllly cosmetic, so doesnt make too much of a difference...?

I'm betting that it will become a problem for some reason later on.

Oh, and I also found a 3D model of the stepper motor I am getting online - just simplifies things a bit for me.

## Current Plan

So as this will be like ideally a fairly simple plotter thing, I plan to now make both the y and x axes the same. Like I'd be able to use the same design, 3D models and mounting hardware between them.

Theoretically I think it should be possible, as they are both essentially just a piece of extrusion with a stepper at the end. Although not quite sure how I will mount it yet.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/62c71e3a43b7dd98af12397dcb6fdd1de6a5f45a24912c363ba4bd6f1b231eec.png)

Don't know if I'll get more done today, but I really do need to try and hurry up to finish it, as I've barely started  the actual models.

Also one thing that looks interesting, is that I might be able to run the stepper motor belts in the actual 2020 extrusion's grooves, and it will all work.

Probably spent a bit too long just researching motion systems and stuff, but I reckon I will just go standard Cartesian over like Core XY - like the kinematics dont seem too difficult, but I just dont think I have the time to be certain a Core XY design would work.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/f13b737564007fe473bfdd1e7724e700b306cf4a4ce67c0eca17840073a5b86d.png)

## tl;dr

Finally started the CAD design, after too much time spent on the BOM.

### 2026-11-08: # CAD

**6.5h**

# CAD

Actually did loads of CAD in this session.

So the design process so far:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/d6ac9b6ee0177eec97b6a8c936b551861c6641768793a5466450344a5d7e0563.png)

I started off by kind of just deleting part of what I made before, then I modelled a rough mounting bits (didn't take intermediary screenshots because I forgot).

I spent a bunch of time deciding how I wanted to place the belts, and I decided to stick with placing them mostly inside the 2020 extrusion.

Also had to look up a bunch of part dimensions to see what would fit, and work where.

Also spent a while figuring out the optimum spacing distance for the POM wheels on the carriage. I ended up with 41.5mm, as that is more or less undersize, but I have some eccentric spacers which can loosen it up if needed.

Had fun making everything on offset planes as well, and making everything update parametrically if say a motor size changed, or the length of the 2020 extrusion changed.

I did initially add parameters, but then I figured that nothing will really change, so I removed them.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/2cdd84bd3d1f0d0a42c19ee8a06c618b7cd4080d7786717484f1da2bab6a243b.png)

So after I made that, single axis bit, I started on the x axis.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/0ba8819403b521fc693842ba730cefbf45e06057b58bb7aa9aa44d694703a858.png)

And as I was trying to make things be like the same between the motor mounts, so there would be less unique pieces, I tried to copy them, but had some intersections, hence the interference analysis above.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/caebce7cf5b66fa6d0559b6c9618b6dad6b498aea5ab9897825a9fa15da2f563.png)

this image you can just see them intersecting - the X axis motor mount (the one on the moving gantry part) clipped into the carriage with that design

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/b61054fc5b30db24c73c19e02aa982e043357a9aad5dbc4c88dc63df18f5fe95.png)

Oh and theres this one which is clearer, after I had to go back and change some other things to make sure everything had the right tolerances,

Also you may notice that between the images above and below, the motor mount is different. This is as originally I was planning to mount the stepper sideways, as I thought that would be the most compact way, but then the belt would interfere with the POM wheels of the X axis carriage.

So that meant I had to mount it vertically. I would have liked to intergrate the mount into the Y carriage, but due to the entire thing being too short, I have to mount it above the X axis.

So it just makes the entire thing a tiny bit taller.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/09969409ea6d822d26398150e9e579b40816b6ebb3a9714ef9b5d5cbcc39e0a7.png)

So currently as many pieces are duplicates as possible - required a bit of redesigning, and doesn't look the best in some places. So will probably not use duplicates for the actual thing.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/7ec189e5eca6ccff3ab909b10030769e6a42a0b1fdcc5cc508680583127aff23.png)

And this image is the latest version after I added the X axis gantry slider.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/2fc816fc87543408c44c1baf583ec566ddad74d2882fc46186788009d858a264.png)

I still need to add the hardware for the pen to go up and down, and for keeping the entire structure upright.

## tl;dr

Did quite a lot of the CAD, mainly the mounting parts for everything.
